paragraphs.source_en: On the night of May 14, the third year of Tenshō, when Torii Suneemon slipped out of Nagashino Castle, Tokugawa Ieyasu had already entered Okazaki Castle and was holding a grand feast. He believed Oda Nobunaga would hurry from Gifu with reinforcements, and intended to clear the obstacles from the path of Nobunaga's great army. Yet even when the feast began, he still did not know whether Nobunaga had set out from Gifu. His retainers, however, held differing opinions.
